paragraphs.text: After the people of God had possessed the land of Canaan in the days of Joshua, they went back and left the commandments of God and entered into idolatrous marriages, so the Gentiles ruled over them and humbled them, and then they cried out to God, and He sent them saviors, the judges, such as Gideon, Jephthah and Samson, who delivered them from their oppressors and brought them back to the worship of God. This shows God's longsuffering, mercies and tenderness toward His people, whom, however much they sinned and returned to Him, He receives and saves. This is especially so since they repeated their disobedience many times: whenever their enemies humbled them and they cried out to God, He delivered them, but they returned again to their negligence and disobedience, so their enemies humbled them, and they cried out to God, who delivered them. Thus God's mercies intervened many times to rescue His disobedient people.

entries.section: (3) The longsuffering of God toward His rebellious people

paragraphs.text: The people of God continued in their sins and their attachment to idolatrous worship, which compelled God to discipline them with the Assyrian captivity and then the Babylonian captivity, that they might repent and return to Him. Thus God's mercies kept seeking His people, by severity and by gentleness, that they might live with Him.

Throughout these periods of disobedience God never tired of sending His prophets to warn His people and rebuke them for their sins. These are the countless mercies of God, who desires the salvation of His children.

God did not deal with His people according to their sins, but bore with them and gave them successive opportunities for repentance. The continuance of His people rests on His divine mercy, for He does not wish to destroy His people as a just punishment for their sins, but wishes them to live with Him, that He may delight them with His blessings.
God's commandments and Law guarantee His children a noble life and joy with God, but leaving them is what exposes them to humiliation and bondage.

entries.section: (4) Confession of sin and making a covenant

paragraphs.text: After the prayer reviewed the mercies of God in the face of the people's disobedience, it now asks the great and awesome God, before whom the hearts of His children are humbled, to look with His tenderness upon His people, who are now humbled in bondage under the hand of the Gentiles, namely Assyria, Babylon, Media and Persia. God had given them the land of Canaan, full of good things, but because of their sins they have come into the humiliation of bondage, dwelling in it, and they have no hope except God, their gracious God, who is able to keep them. Thus feelings of the fear of God are mingled with hope, for He is at once the awesome and the gracious God, in whom His people hope.

This prayer shows the people's confession of their sins, themselves, their fathers and their kings, and their acknowledgment of the grace of God, His mercies and His longsuffering. It is a contrite prayer that calls forth the mercies of God.

At the end of the prayer the people show the extent of the distress they suffer and that they do not benefit from the good things of the land, for these go to the kings while they are in hard bondage, scarcely obtaining their food, and all the good things go to the king, so their bodies have become humbled like those of slaves.

entries.section: (4) Confession of sin and making a covenant

paragraphs.text: The prayer ended with a definite positive act, namely the making of a covenant with God, which all the people declared and the priests and Levites, that is, the spiritual leaders of the people, confirmed. It is understood implicitly that this covenant included holding fast to the commandments and Law of God and keeping away from idolatrous worship and all evil.

To confirm the covenant, the people wrote it down so that it might be a witness against them and a declaration that they did not wish to turn back from it by their free will. Then a number of the priests and Levites came forward and sealed this written covenant, as a declaration on their part that they were responsible for carrying out this covenant and for always urging the people to hold fast to it. Thus we see that the long prayer before had a strong effect in making a firm and lasting covenant with God. By this the prophecy of Jeremiah was fulfilled that the people of God after the captivity would “join themselves to the LORD in a perpetual covenant that shall not be forgotten” (Jer 50:5).

May you turn your spiritual feelings into definite exercises that help you in life with God, so that you strive in the spiritual way by rejecting the beloved sin and holding fast to the spiritual practices that bring you near to God, such as prayer, fasting and reading the Holy Bible, and from them result your love and service to God. Renewal of the covenant

entries.section: (1) The sealing of the covenant

paragraphs.text: It mentions Nehemiah and the chief priests who sealed, twenty-two in number, although the chief priests number twenty-four, as the prophet David arranged. Perhaps two of the chief priests were prevented by circumstances of illness from being present and taking part in sealing the covenant. The priests sealed first, after Nehemiah, to be an example to those after them.

entries.section: (1) The sealing of the covenant

paragraphs.text: It mentions the heads of the Levites who sealed the covenant, 17 in number. Their order comes after the priests in the covenant because they are helpers of the priests in the service of the house of the Lord and are responsible with them for teaching the people. Most of these Levites taught the people and explained the book of the Law (ch. 9:4-5).

entries.section: (1) The sealing of the covenant

paragraphs.text: After the Levites, the leaders of the people came forward, forty-four in number, and sealed the covenant, declaring their responsibility for leading the people in holding fast to the terms of this covenant. Most of these leaders were mentioned in (ch. 7:8). The Holy Bible mentions many times the renewal of the covenant with God, as happened in the days of Moses (Ex 24:5-7), in the days of King Asa (2 Chr 15:12, 13), likewise in the days of King Hezekiah (2 Chr 29:10), and then in the days of Ezra the priest (Ezra 10:30). This shows that the people of God turned back from their covenant with God many times, and God was longsuffering toward them, until Christ came and secured the covenant by His blood and gave us salvation in His Church through the Holy Sacraments.

Here we see Nehemiah's concern that the spiritual leaders and the leaders of the people should seal the covenant, so that they would be responsible for leading the people in holding fast to the covenant.

When you make any spiritual vows before God, be assured that this gladdens the heart of God. So take care on every occasion in your life to offer vows to God in order to live with Him, and let them be definite vows, and may you follow them up at intervals, such as every day and every week.

entries.section: (2) Those who pledged themselves and the terms of the covenant

paragraphs.text: All classes of the people agreed to this covenant, which the priests, the Levites and the leaders sealed, that they might hold fast to everything in the covenant. Men and women took part in this agreement, and also the children, together with all those who worked in the Temple. The agreement of the children shows us the importance of caring for them. Therefore the Church in the New Testament has taken care to bring children into the covenant of God through the sacrament of Baptism under the care of their parents.
Those who agreed were not only the Jews, but those who had joined them from the Gentiles, and this is a type of God's receiving the Gentiles into the New Covenant together with the Jews.

This covenant was between two parties: the first party is God, and the second party is the people, represented by Nehemiah, the priests, the Levites and the leaders, followed by all the people in their different classes.
All classes of the people took part in this covenant, because all had sinned; therefore all should pledge themselves to a new life with God.

It says, “they that had separated themselves from the people of the lands ... every one having knowledge, and having understanding,” that is, those who had come of age and had mental understanding and acceptance of the Law of God. What is meant by those having knowledge and understanding may be those whose hearts were opened to know God, so they believed and understood and joined the people of God. Those who joined from the peoples of the lands declared their faith by word of mouth, by oath and swearing, and perhaps also by raising the hand. This oath and swearing means obtaining God's blessings if they held fast to the terms of the covenant, and their deserving of a curse when they broke the covenant. And their oath was to keep all the commandments.
Moses is called here the servant of God because of his great standing and his belonging to God, for he was faithful in his life with God and his service to Him.

entries.section: (2) Those who pledged themselves and the terms of the covenant

paragraphs.text: The covenant included seven terms. The first was not to intermarry with the idolatrous peoples surrounding the people of God in the whole world, as the Law prescribed (Deut 7:3-4). The people of God were exposed to falling into this sin from the days of Moses and Joshua, and even after their return from the captivity they fell into this sin. It is a hard sin, because it leads to the worship of idols, and because of its seriousness it is mentioned as the first of the terms of the covenant. The believer's love for all people does not mean that he is lax toward sin and intermarries with unbelievers; rather he must hold fast to his faith and his spiritual teachings with all exactness.

The second term is keeping the Sabbath day, as God said (Ex 23:10-11, Lev 25:2). It is a holy day for the worship of God every week, on which no work is done, and therefore trading with the Gentiles on it is refused. The gates of Jerusalem and the Jewish cities were closed on it to prevent trade with foreigners. By this the believer declares his holding fast to the worship of God and refuses the material gain that would hinder him on the day of the Lord.

The third term in the covenant is the sanctification of the holy days, that is, the feasts and the spiritual seasons, and also the seventh year, the sabbath of the years, as God commanded them (Lev 26:34, 35), in which the Jews set free their brothers who had been enslaved to them and waived the debts owed to them by their brothers.

entries.section: (2) Those who pledged themselves and the terms of the covenant

paragraphs.text: The fourth term in the covenant was the obligation of every man who reached the age of twenty years (Ex 30:13-14) to pay for the service of the Temple a third of a shekel of silver (Ex 30:16). A third of a shekel equals about 4 grams of silver. The Law required the man to pay half a shekel, but because of the hard economic circumstances through which the people of God were passing, since they were slaves and the goods of the land were taken by the king, they neglected payment to the Temple. Here they returned and offered a third of a shekel yearly, because of their extreme poverty. Nehemiah the governor did not compel the people to pay a sum to the Temple, but they bound themselves, out of their love for God. This sum was paid by the poor like the rich, to declare that the worth of each one is equal before God. Despite the smallness of the offering, because it came from all the people it sufficed for the needs of the Temple and its servants, such as the cost of the daily burnt offerings and the sacrifices offered at the seasons, and so on.

It is understood implicitly that there was no money in the Temple; the treasury was empty, and there was no Jewish king to help the Temple from his own funds, so the need was pressing that the people should pay a contribution to the Temple as the Law indicated. A similar situation had happened in ancient times in the days of King Joash, who encouraged the people to pay the contribution to the Temple and used the silver collected in restoring the Temple and organizing its service (2 Chr 24:

entries.section: (2) Those who pledged themselves and the terms of the covenant

paragraphs.text: The group of the Nethinim, who were a company of Gentiles who joined the people of God in the days of Joshua, had as their service the gathering of wood for the service of the Temple. But only a small number of them returned from the captivity, not enough to gather the wood required for the Temple, so the people considered how to arrange and gather the wood, and agreed that it should fall on families of the priests, the Levites and the people, and that these families should be chosen by lot, to receive the blessing of this service. This was the fifth term of the covenant, namely the offering of the wood.

entries.section: (2) Those who pledged themselves and the terms of the covenant

paragraphs.text: The sixth term of the covenant is the people's obligation to offer the firstfruits of their crops, whether plants or trees, and the firstfruits of the dough, and the firstborn of the animals, and also the firstborn of the sons of the people, or to offer silver for them to the Temple (Ex 13:2; Num 3:46). All these firstborn were offered to the priests.

Thus the people feel that God takes the firstborn of everything to bless the rest, and so they feel the hand of God with them. And the beautiful thing is that they commit themselves to all this despite their poverty, for giving out of want has great value before God, and of course God enriches them and blesses them more than they gave.

entries.section: (2) Those who pledged themselves and the terms of the covenant

paragraphs.text: The seventh term in the covenant is the obligation to offer the tithes to the Levites, who in turn tithe what they have received, giving the tenth to the priests. Thus the storehouses of the Temple are filled with gifts, to be food for the priests and all who work in the Temple.

Offering tithes and firstfruits to God is love, in response to His love, which began and continues with us, for it is He who redeemed us and gave us His life and still takes care of us. May we always thank Him and express our love for Him, so that we gladden His heart and our hearts rejoice with Him.
The repopulating of Jerusalem

entries.section: (2) Those who dwelt in Jerusalem

paragraphs.text: It mentions the classes that dwelt in Jerusalem, which it will mention in detail in the following verses. In Jerusalem dwelt the rulers of the land, and also those chosen by lot from the tribes of Judah and Benjamin, in addition to those chosen from the priests, the Levites, the Nethinim and the children of Solomon's servants, whose dwelling was necessary for the service of the Temple, so they dwelt beside it in Jerusalem. It does not give the details of the names and numbers of the children of Solomon's servants, who joined the people of God and helped in the service.

entries.section: (2) Those who dwelt in Jerusalem

paragraphs.text: Of the children of Judah there dwelt four hundred and sixty-eight persons, all of them of the children of Pharez, from whose seed Christ came.

The number of the members of the tribe of Judah was less than that of the tribe of Benjamin, but they were men of valor, so they were suitable for guarding the city, as we heard of the seed of Judah from ancient times, “Judah is a lion's whelp” (Gen 49:9), that is, he is very strong.

entries.section: (2) Those who dwelt in Jerusalem

paragraphs.text: Of the children of Benjamin there dwelt nine hundred and twenty-eight persons, a number greater than that of the tribe of Judah, because in Jerusalem Benjamin had a larger share than Judah.
It mentions an overseer of the Benjamites and an assistant to him, and this means that Nehemiah ordered them to organize their ranks for ease of governing them and guarding the city.

entries.section: (2) Those who dwelt in Jerusalem

paragraphs.text: The priests were chosen from three houses, or clans, to dwell in Jerusalem, and the Holy Bible describes them as men of valor, distinguished in bodily strength, because the service of the priesthood, especially at the beginning of the restoration of the Temple, required no little effort.

The number of the priests was one thousand one hundred and ninety-two priests, which is a large number, and this shows the concern of the priests to return from the captivity for the service of the Temple, and they dwelt beside it in Jerusalem.

entries.section: (2) Those who dwelt in Jerusalem

paragraphs.text: The number of the Levites was two hundred and forty-two, a small number compared with the priests, because some of them lived in the various lands to carry out the service of teaching the people the worship of God and the keeping of His commandments. It mentions that two of the Levites were responsible for the outward work of the Temple, such as collecting contributions or the materials needed for the service of the Temple, or teaching the people.

It also mentions two who were responsible for praise, and they were of the seed of the chief of the singers, Asaph and Jeduthun. This shows the concern in the Temple for praise and prayers, which must be joined with thanksgiving. It mentions that the number of the gatekeepers was one hundred and seventy-two, and this shows the concern for guarding the Temple, apart from the guarding of the city of Jerusalem.

We notice that it speaks of the people of God and calls them Israel, for the second time in this chapter (v. 3), because when the people of God returned from the captivity they were one unit, and the division that existed in ancient times before the captivity, namely the two kingdoms of Israel and Judah, was gone; after the captivity they became one kingdom called Israel, including all the tribes, Judah among them.

The Nethinim helped in the service of the Temple. They were the seed of the Gibeonites, of the Gentiles and not of the Jews, and they had joined the people of God in the days of Joshua. They dwelt in special dwellings in Ophel, which is a hill beside the wall of Jerusalem, at the Water Gate, to make their work easy for them, which was bringing water for the needs of the Temple.

entries.section: (2) Those who dwelt in Jerusalem

paragraphs.text: The Levites had a chief and an overseer for them, who dwelt in Jerusalem and took care of managing the affairs of the Levites dwelling in Jerusalem or outside it, and they referred to him in every counsel. He was distinguished in leadership although he was one of the singers, but because of his administrative excellence he became the overseer of all the Levites.

The singers had been working for King Artaxerxes in the Persian capital, and when they came with Nehemiah, the king ordered that they should receive their allowances from the king while they were in Jerusalem, in return for offering supplications and prayers for him before the house of the Lord.

entries.section: (2) Those who dwelt in Jerusalem

paragraphs.text: The Persian king Artaxerxes appointed an agent for himself in Jerusalem to collect the taxes, pay out of them what the Temple needed, and send the rest to the royal palace. It was a beautiful providence of God that the king chose this agent from the Jews, so that he would be compassionate toward them and not exploit them or steal from these funds for himself. All the numbers mentioned here of the Jews amount to two thousand six hundred and thirty-eight, apart from the leaders and the children of Solomon's servants, and also the Jews who had been in Jerusalem before Nehemiah. Although this number was small, God blessed them, so the city was rebuilt and multiplied within 400 years until Christ became incarnate, when the city was full of inhabitants.

How beautiful is the repopulating of the holy city, and better than it is the filling of the Church with worshipers. So take care to attend church regularly and encourage your loved ones, that all may receive a blessing and gladden the heart of God.

entries.section: (3) The dwelling places of Judah and Benjamin outside Jerusalem

paragraphs.text: It tells us about the towns in which the tribe of Judah dwelt in Judea, that is, around Jerusalem. They were mentioned before in (Josh 15).

entries.section: (3) The dwelling places of Judah and Benjamin outside Jerusalem

paragraphs.text: It mentions here the towns in which the tribe of Benjamin dwelt outside Jerusalem.

entries.section: (3) The dwelling places of Judah and Benjamin outside Jerusalem

paragraphs.text: It points out to us here that the tribes of Judah and Benjamin took care to set apart places for the Levites to dwell among them, as Joshua the son of Nun commanded, and by this they carry out their role in teaching the people and guiding them.
Give a place of your time and attention to listening to the teachings of God from the mouth of the priests and deacons, and you will receive a blessing and walk in the way of the Kingdom.

The priesthood and the dedication of the wall. The book of Nehemiah presents to us the building of the wall of Jerusalem and how the resistance of the wicked was overcome, then tells us of the religious reform through the reading of the book of the Law, then the renewal of the covenant with God, and after this tells us of the dedication of the wall. But it did not fix the date of the dedication of the wall: was it done at the end of the twelve years that Nehemiah spent in Jerusalem, before his return to Shushan, the palace, the capital of the empire, or before this?

And in this chapter, before explaining to us how the wall was dedicated, it tells us of the list of the priests and Levites who came with Zerubbabel and down to the days of the dedication of the wall, because of the importance of the role of the priests and Levites in worship and dedication.

entries.section: (1) The priests and Levites who returned from the captivity

paragraphs.text: Nehemiah takes care to set down these lists of the priests, followed by the Levites, in honor of them for their faithfulness, and on the other hand so that this may always be an incentive to the priests and Levites who serve in his days in the Temple to do their service with faithfulness and spiritual zeal. There is also the greatness of these leaders, for they left the powerful land of the captivity and came to Jerusalem in ruins, for the sake of God and His worship.

It mentions to us the chief priests who returned with Zerubbabel in 536 BC to Jerusalem; they were only four chiefs (Ezra 2:36-39), but Zerubbabel divided them into 22 courses, whereas the prophet David had divided the priests into 24 courses (1 Chr 24:8). Jeshua, mentioned in (v. 1), is the supreme head of all the priests.
Abijah, mentioned in (v. 4), is the ancestor of John the Baptist (Lk 1:5).

entries.section: (1) The priests and Levites who returned from the captivity

paragraphs.text: It mentions to us the Levites responsible for works in the Temple, which are:
1- Thanksgiving, or praise, that is, chanting the Psalms.
2- Guarding the gates of the Temple.

entries.section: (1) The priests and Levites who returned from the captivity

paragraphs.text: It gives us a list of the names of the high priests throughout the period of Persian rule, beginning with Jeshua, who returned from the captivity with Zerubbabel, down to Jehoiada, who was in the days of Nehemiah, and whose grandson was also called Jaddua. He is the one who received Alexander the Great in the year 322 BC, wearing his priestly garments, and informed him of the prophecy of Daniel concerning the rise of the Greek empire. Alexander had seen the appearance of this priest in a dream the night before, so there came to be goodwill between Alexander and the Jews. He considered that the God of Israel blessed his steps, and so he drew back from conquering Jerusalem. All this is reported from Josephus the historian. It is noted that this list does not contain all the high priests, but some were omitted.

entries.section: (1) The priests and Levites who returned from the captivity

paragraphs.text: Here it mentions a list of the chief priests who were in the days of Nehemiah, each of whom represented a course of the priests, and it mentions his great-grandfather, who was in the days of Zerubbabel, such as “Of Seraiah, Meraiah”: Seraiah was the chief priest in the days of Zerubbabel (v. 1) and Meraiah his grandson was the chief priest in the days of Nehemiah (v. 12...), and so on.

Here Nehemiah takes care to mention the chief priests, to whom history began to be ascribed after the captivity, when they had no king; for anciently, before the captivity, history was ascribed to the kings of Judah and Israel.

entries.section: (1) The priests and Levites who returned from the captivity

paragraphs.text: Here it mentions with care the Levites as heads of fathers' houses in the days of Eliashib the high priest in the time of Nehemiah's governorship of Jerusalem. This is because the role of the priests had grown weak in this period and the role of the Levites in the service had grown strong, so they were counted as heads of fathers' houses. Their role was shown in the explanation of the Law in (ch. 8:7) and the leading of prayer (ch. 9:4, 5), for God does not leave Himself without a witness.

Some courses of the Levites were responsible for praise, and each course was divided so that it had its turn, that is, a part in which it carried out the praise before the Temple of God. Perhaps the course was divided into two sections, one chanting a portion of the Psalm and the other responding to it according to the command of David (1 Chr 23:30). There were also other courses of the Levites for guarding.

How great it is that you carry out your service, for it is precious in the eyes of God because it is offered out of love for Him. Do not be distracted from it by the vain affairs of life, as the priests were distracted in the days of Nehemiah. God did not forsake His people when the Levites rose with zeal to serve His house, and He will send someone to care for them, but you will lose the blessing.

entries.section: (2) The dedication of the wall of Jerusalem

paragraphs.text: Dedication: consecrating or setting apart a place or a thing to God by special prayers.

Nehemiah took care to gather the Levites from all the places in which they dwelt around Jerusalem, to come and take part in the dedication of the wall. They had returned to their places after keeping the Feast of Tabernacles, and it was necessary to summon them to share with the priests and the people in this dedication, for the dedication is not proper without the servants appointed for it.
The dedication of the wall was important for the following reasons:
1- To thank God, who helped them and completed the building for them.
2- To acknowledge that God is the protector of Jerusalem by His blessing of the wall.
3- The city of Jerusalem and its wall are dedicated to God, and it is not proper that any work against God be done in it, such as the worship of idols.
The dedication is a joyful act, and so it was accompanied by musical instruments with words of praise, and all were in joy because of the great work of God with them.

entries.section: (2) The dedication of the wall of Jerusalem

paragraphs.text: Before entering into the rite of dedication, all who took part in it had to be purified, and those who carried out the purification were the priests and Levites, who purified the people, the wall and the gates. Therefore the priest and the servant must be purified by cleansing his heart, and by repentance, before undertaking any service.

The purification of a person is by sprinkling the water of purification, as the Law of Moses commanded (Num 8:7; 19:9), and the purification of the wall and the gates is by sprinkling the water of purification upon it.
This purification signifies, in the New Testament, the examining of the soul, repentance and confession, so that a person may be able to approach to partake of the Holy Mysteries.

entries.section: (2) The dedication of the wall of Jerusalem

paragraphs.text: “Went”: it walked at a slow pace.

Nehemiah divided the priests, the Levites and the rulers into two companies. One company, led by Ezra the priest, went from the south of Jerusalem toward the northeast until it reached the Temple, which lies in the north of Jerusalem; it walked to the right on the wall, that is, counterclockwise. The second company moved from the south of Jerusalem and walked on top of the wall toward the west and then the north until it reached the Temple; that is, it walked to the left on the wall, clockwise. Thus the two companies moved from one place and met at the end at the Temple, because the wall was great in length and therefore needed two companies, the first under the hand of Ezra and the second under the leadership of Nehemiah himself. This means that the wall was broad enough to allow rows of people to walk on it side by side.
We see Nehemiah's humility: he walks behind his company, but he put Ezra at the head of the second company in honor of him.
And the people walked on the ground inside the walls of Jerusalem, praying and chanting the Psalms of David alongside the company with which they walked.
In these verses we see that Nehemiah placed corresponding groups in each of the two companies, as the following table shows:
A table showing the two companies that carried out the dedication of the wall. The first company. The second company
1- Led by Ezra. 1- Nehemiah behind it
2- The company of the singers of praise. 2- The company of the singers of praise
3- Half of the princes of Judah. 3- Half of the rulers
4- The sons of the priests with trumpets. 4- The priests with trumpets
5- Seven priests from Azariah to Jeremiah. 5- Seven priests from Eliakim to Hananiah
6- Bearers of the instruments of song (the musicians). 6- The singers

7- Zechariah and eight others. 7- Jezrahiah and eight others. Thus the dedication of the wall was completed by passing over all of it and sprinkling all of it with water, it and its gates, and prayers went up over it. The conclusion was the meeting of all who took part in the dedication, with the people behind them, in the Temple, and there they prayed and thanked God and offered sacrifices of thanksgiving, as we shall see in the following verses.

entries.section: (2) The dedication of the wall of Jerusalem

paragraphs.text: The people offered many sacrifices to God on the day of the dedication of the wall, expressing their coming to God, their sacrifice for Him and their thanksgiving to Him, because He:
1- Helped them and completed the wall for them, to protect their city.
2- Brought to nothing the plots of the wicked who tried to hinder the building of the wall.
3- Filled their city with inhabitants.

4- Gave them unity in the meeting of the civil leaders, that is, Nehemiah and all his assistants, with the spiritual leaders, who are the priests and Levites. And all were of one spirit with the people.

All that preceded expressed their feelings and filled them with joy. And when God saw their concern, which included all, men, women and children, He gave them a special grace of divine joy, which surpassed all their imagining, so that their joy was in truth a great joy.
And their strong joy appeared in a shout in a loud voice from all the people, so that it was heard from afar from Jerusalem, the holy city.

Be faithful in your responsibilities for the sake of God, and your heart will rejoice in His grace; for when you offer your feelings toward Him you receive an abundance of His love, and He gives you what He gives to no one else, namely peace and happiness, which are the pledge of the Kingdom of Heaven.

entries.section: (3) The portions of the priests and Levites

paragraphs.text: The chambers: the rooms attached to the Temple.

The offerings (heave offerings): everything that a person lifts up from his produce or his earnings to God, that is, the contributions, the tithes and what exceeds them, for he felt that what he offered was lifted up to God who dwells in heaven.
The firstfruits: the first produce.

The people expressed their joy in God who dwelt in their midst and who completed the wall for them, so they offered all that the Law prescribed of tithes and firstfruits, and also all that exceeded it of offerings of love for God. They appointed priests and Levites in charge of the storehouses in which were gathered the various offerings of the people, which they collected from the cities of the children of Israel. Perhaps they set aside special rooms for each city; that is, they established a careful system for collecting the gifts that were used in the Temple and from which portions were given to the Levites.
What is meant by “that day” is at that time, and not a specific day, for in those days the people's faithfulness in offering their gifts to the Temple appeared.

May you express your joy not by mere emotion, but by making decisions and offering the love of God in your relationship with Him and in your service in His Church, and so your joy will be firm and you will gladden the heart of God.

entries.section: (3) The portions of the priests and Levites

paragraphs.text: The priests and Levites also expressed their joy by the following:
1- Appointing overseers over the storehouses, as the previous verse mentioned.

2- Keeping watch at the gates of the Temple to prevent the entrance of foreigners from the Gentiles, or of the unclean; this is the ward of purification, that is, making sure of the purity and readiness of everyone who enters the Temple.

3- The singers carrying out their role in chanting the Psalms before the Temple, by organizing companies that took turns in their work, to offer constant prayers before God, and so that those entering the Temple might enjoy sharing in these prayers. This is what David and Solomon commanded, and Nehemiah and Ezra now restored it.

entries.section: (3) The portions of the priests and Levites

paragraphs.text: To organize the companies of singers, David anciently appointed chiefs of the singers, such as Asaph, and now in the days of Nehemiah and Ezra they too appointed chiefs of the singers, to organize the service of praise and glorification, that is, thanksgiving in the Temple.

entries.section: (3) The portions of the priests and Levites

paragraphs.text: We see the clear concern for the service of the Temple after the return from the captivity, that is, in the days of Zerubbabel and then in the days of Nehemiah, the governors who ruled over Jerusalem and Judea. They took care to provide for the material needs of the singers and gatekeepers; perhaps they assigned larger gifts to these two classes than to the rest of the Levites, and singing and guarding may have been a work in addition to sharing in the rest of the works of the Levites, which confirms that these two classes deserved larger gifts.

We see a clear concern on the part of the Levites, to whom the people give tithes and various gifts, for they in turn offer their tithes and gifts to the priests. Thus all enjoy, not only the provision of the needs of others, but, more important than this, the receiving of God's blessing in their lives.

The word “sanctify” expresses God's blessing upon all that a person possesses. He who gives tithes and gifts to God, God sanctifies all the rest that he has, so that it suffices him and overflows. The gift is a blessing to the one who gives, as it is to the one who receives, and all blessing is from the hand of God.

How beautiful it is that the Levites take care of the needs of their spiritual fathers, who are the priests, as the people took care of the needs of their spiritual guides, who are the Levites. For if all the spiritual leaders care for the spiritual needs of the people, then all the more should the people care to provide for their material needs, so that they lack nothing and are not occupied with anything away from their service, which is the most important work, as the Apostle Paul affirmed (1 Cor 9:11). Renewed purification. Nehemiah spent twelve years in Jerusalem (ch. 5:14), in which he completed the building of the wall and the spiritual care of the people, and perhaps he returned to the king once or several times in this period, but nothing is mentioned about that in the Holy Bible.

After twelve years Nehemiah returned to the king and spent a period with him whose length is not known; it may have been months or years. After it he returned to Jerusalem, because his heart was attached to it, and was surprised by the spread of evil among the people. Since Nehemiah was concerned not only with the outward fortification of Jerusalem but rather with the care of the people, his heart was deeply moved when he found them fallen into many sins, the most important of which were:
1- Mingling with the Ammonites and Moabites.
2- Defiling the Temple by bringing the Gentiles into it.
3- Neglecting to collect the tithes, and so the Levites did not find their food and left the service of the Temple, and worship stopped in the Temple.
4- Breaking the Sabbath day.
5- Marrying idolatrous women and so becoming attached to their gods.

Despite all these corruptions Nehemiah did not despair but trusted in God and began to purify the people again and bring them back to God. What, then, were the second reforms that Nehemiah carried out?
(1) The expulsion of the Ammonites and Moabites (vv. 1-9)

1- On that day they read in the book of Moses in the audience of the people; and therein was found written, that the Ammonite and the Moabite should not come into the congregation of God for ever; 2- Because they met not the children of Israel with bread and with water, but hired Balaam against them, that he should curse them: howbeit our God turned the curse into a blessing. 3- Now it came to pass, when they had heard the law, that they separated from Israel all the mixed multitude. 4- And before this, Eliashib the priest, having the oversight of the chamber of the house of our God, was allied unto Tobiah: 5- And he had prepared for him a great chamber, where aforetime they laid the meat offerings, the frankincense, and the vessels, and the tithes of the corn, the new wine, and the oil, which was commanded to be given to the Levites, and the singers, and the porters; and the offerings of the priests. 6- But in all this time was not I at Jerusalem: for in the two and thirtieth year of Artaxerxes king of Babylon came I unto the king, and after certain days obtained I leave of the king:

7- And I came to Jerusalem, and understood of the evil that Eliashib did for Tobiah, in preparing him a chamber in the courts of the house of God. 8- And it grieved me sore: therefore I cast forth all the household stuff of Tobiah out of the chamber. 9- Then I commanded, and they cleansed the chambers: and thither brought I again the vessels of the house of God, with the meat offering and the frankincense.

entries.section: (3) The portions of the priests and Levites

paragraphs.text: The mixed multitude: the Gentiles who went with the children of Israel and dwelt among them and did not join the faith of the Jews. Among them were a great number of Moabites and Ammonites, who lived adjoining the people of God.

Before beginning his reforms, Nehemiah took care to read the Holy Bible publicly to the people assembled before him in the Temple. By the providence of God, on that day they read in the twenty-third chapter of the book of Deuteronomy, and found written in it that the Law commands keeping away from the Ammonites and Moabites, because they bear enmity to the children of Israel and so draw them to the worship of their gods (Deut 23:3-5). The people responded to the word of God and obeyed the Law, so they separated and put out from among them all the Moabites and Ammonites, and by this they got rid of what caused them to stumble and kept them far from God. The text of the Law here does not intend racial discrimination, but keeping away from evil and from the evil association that causes the children of God to fall and separates them from Him, just as the tribe of Reuben housed the Moabites in its midst, and they led the Jews in the worship of Chemosh their god, and moreover enslaved them under the leadership of Eglon their king for eighteen years. God permitted strangers who join the faith in Him to offer sacrifices to Him (Num 15:14) and received Ruth the Moabitess into His people, so that she married Boaz, and moreover Christ came from her seed.

entries.section: (3) The portions of the priests and Levites

paragraphs.text: As a result of the negligence of the priests and their marriage to foreign women from the Gentiles, there was a kinship between Eliashib the high priest and Tobiah the Ammonite, who had resisted the building of the wall, and this formed a friendship between them. So when matters had calmed and years had passed after the building of the wall, Tobiah was able by his influence to persuade Eliashib the high priest to set aside for him a large room in the Temple, in which to stay when he visited Jerusalem. This room had been set apart for storing the contributions offered by the people, namely the incense and the vessels of the Temple, and also the people's tithes of wheat, wine and oil, which were distributed to the Levites and the priests. So Eliashib emptied the room and prepared it as a dwelling for Tobiah his relative, although the Law forbids the entrance of the Gentiles into the Temple, and especially the Ammonites (v. 1; Deut 23:3). How then could Tobiah enter and dwell there?
Thus we see Eliashib's great negligence in two matters:
1- Bringing Tobiah into the Temple to dwell beside it, as a result of the kinship between them, defying God and His Law.
2- His neglect of the needs of the Levites and the equipment of the Temple, for he took out everything that was in the storehouses, which exposed it to spoiling.
Perhaps his preparing “the great chamber” for Tobiah was done by buying splendid furniture, or by joining several rooms together to be a dwelling worthy of Tobiah his relative.

entries.section: (3) The portions of the priests and Levites

paragraphs.text: This great error into which Eliashib fell happened during the absence of Nehemiah with King Artaxerxes. Eliashib seized the opportunity of Nehemiah's not being in Jerusalem, and honored Tobiah at the expense of the house of God. Perhaps intermarriage had taken place between the seed of Eliashib and the seed of Tobiah in this period, and visits, exchange of gifts and honors took place between them, among them this honor of preparing a chamber for Tobiah in the Temple. This shows the importance of the presence of the spiritual leader, for Nehemiah represented the truth and the voice of God, and the people and the priests feared him, although it should have been Eliashib the high priest who was the spiritual leader, who proclaims the fear of God and the necessity of holding fast to His Law. This reminds us of the sin of Aaron when he made the golden calf in the period of Moses' absence on the mountain to receive God's commandments and Law (Ex 32:4). As for Nehemiah's return to the king in the thirty-second year of the reign of Artaxerxes, that is, after twelve years he had spent in Jerusalem, it was either because of an appointed time agreed upon with the king at which he would return to Babylon, or because the king summoned Nehemiah to be reassured about the condition of Jerusalem and Judea, over which Nehemiah was governor on behalf of the king.

Hold fast to the truth and the commandments of God, even if those around you draw away from them. By this you protect yourself from the wars of the devil, enjoy the care of God and are a light to the world. And God gives you awe in the eyes of others, even if they pretend to resist you or mock you, for the power of God that is in you will affect their hearts.

entries.section: (3) The portions of the priests and Levites

paragraphs.text: Nehemiah was greatly distressed when he saw the defilement of the Temple by the dwelling of Tobiah the pagan inside it, and the negligence of Eliashib, who should have been the first to defend the Temple and be careful for its purity. So he came forward with courage, not fearing the influence of Tobiah nor the authority of Eliashib the high priest, and took out all Tobiah's belongings and threw them outside the Temple. Then he commanded, and the priests purified the chamber in which Tobiah had dwelt, as the Law requires. After that he brought back into the chamber the vessels of the house of the Lord, the incense and all the gifts that the people had offered to the Temple to be a portion for the Levites.
We notice here several things:

1- When Eliashib was negligent, Nehemiah came forward and did what Eliashib should have done. He did not keep silent, although he was the governor and not the high priest, but took care to carry out the Law, since the high priest had been negligent.

2- Nehemiah did not take Tobiah's belongings for himself, but wished to be rid of them by throwing them outside the Temple, so that Eliashib or Tobiah might take them, but that they might not defile the Temple of God. In this he resembles Christ, who drove the sellers out of the Temple, them and all their belongings, that the house of God might remain a house of prayer (Mt 21:13).
3- Nehemiah's care for the needs of the priests and Levites, so that they would not be hindered from their service of the Temple.
4- His honoring of the vessels of the house of the Lord and its needs of incense and the like.

If a person falls into sin, he must be rid of all its sources and purify himself by repentance and confession, so that he can approach to partake of the Holy Mysteries and his heart becomes a dwelling for God alone; as Nehemiah got rid of Tobiah's belongings and purified the chamber, and then brought the vessels of the house of the Lord and the gifts of the people into the chamber.
(2) Collecting the tithes (vv. 10-14)

10- And I perceived that the portions of the Levites had not been given them: for the Levites and the singers, that did the work, were fled every one to his field. 11- Then contended I with the rulers, and said, Why is the house of God forsaken? And I gathered them together, and set them in their place.

12- Then brought all Judah the tithe of the corn and the new wine and the oil unto the treasuries. 13- And I made treasurers over the treasuries, Shelemiah the priest, and Zadok the scribe, and of the Levites, Pedaiah: and next to them was Hanan the son of Zaccur, the son of Mattaniah: for they were counted faithful, and their office was to distribute unto their brethren. 14- Remember me, O my God, concerning this, and wipe not out my good deeds that I have done for the house of my God, and for the offices thereof.

entries.section: (3) The portions of the priests and Levites

paragraphs.text: When Nehemiah entered the Temple to purify it of Tobiah's belongings, he noticed the absence of the Levites from the Temple; he did not hear the praise of the singers, and he learned that the people no longer offered their tithes and gifts in the Temple. The reason may have been that the people knew that their gifts had been thrown out of the Temple to prepare a chamber for Tobiah, or that Tobiah had also seized them, so they no longer offered their offerings. As a result the Levites did not find what they needed and were compelled to go to the fields to work in them so as to find their food, and they left the service of the house of the Lord. What is strange is that none of this concerned Eliashib the high priest, because of his being absorbed in honoring Tobiah, nor did it concern the rulers, that is, the leaders of the people, who were occupied with their positions; perhaps they fell into the sin of seizing part of the portions of the Levites, and the gifts were divided between the priests and the rulers. In short, the Levites did not find their food, so they looked for other work to meet their needs.

entries.section: (3) The portions of the priests and Levites

paragraphs.text: The first reform that Nehemiah carried out was that he stood as an adversary to the rulers and rebuked them because they had not stood against Eliashib and had left the gifts of the Temple to be thrown outside the storehouses, so that the people doubted whether their gifts reached the Levites, and they did not encourage the people to return to paying the tithes. His second reform was that he sent and called Levites from every place in Judea and gathered them to the Temple, and set each one of them in his service according to the arrangement that had been in force before he traveled to the king, and by this the service returned to the Temple as it had been.

It is noticed that he did not rebuke the Levites, because they were excusable, for they were compelled to look for their food by working in the fields. It was not their intention to leave the service of the Temple, but the error of Eliashib and the error of the people toward them, as we mentioned, drove them to leave the Temple. Nehemiah was positive: although he did not blame them for leaving the service, he brought them back to their service, and so they gave up their attachment to the fields and material gain; that is, he restored them to devote themselves to the service of God.

entries.section: (3) The portions of the priests and Levites

paragraphs.text: The rulers, the assistants of Nehemiah, that is, the leaders of the people, moved and called the people to offer the tithes and contributions to the Temple, as they had formerly pledged (ch. 10:39). They were encouraged when they saw the zeal of Nehemiah, faithful for the house of the Lord, and they offered their gifts of wheat, wine and oil.

entries.section: (3) The portions of the priests and Levites

paragraphs.text: To organize the collection of the people's gifts and their distribution to the priests and Levites, Nehemiah appointed a group of priests and Levites known for faithfulness, accuracy and bearing responsibility, and gave them the responsibility of the storehouses in the Temple. This is the third reform that Nehemiah carried out, and it shows his excellence in administration and the organization of works.

entries.section: (3) The portions of the priests and Levites

paragraphs.text: In all that he did, Nehemiah did not look for a reward from anyone, but did everything for God's sake. He is a man of prayer, and he ended what he did in the preceding verses with a prayer in which he asked God to remember him with mercy for the forgiveness of his sins, and he besought God not to forget any good deed he had done by the power of God in Jerusalem, such as the building of the wall.

What has gone before and what comes in this chapter show the importance of the leader in leading others to obey God and His commandments. In Nehemiah's presence great achievements were made, which we saw in the first twelve chapters of this book, but when he was absent for a little while with the king, the people returned to their sins and negligence. Yet by the grace of God and the faithfulness of Nehemiah they returned again to God, as appears from this chapter.

Be careful to hold fast to the commandments of God and to fulfill your responsibilities, because you are responsible for those around you: your drawing near to God brings them near to Him, and your drawing away from Him makes them stumble and draws them away from Him.
(3) Keeping the Sabbath (vv. 15-22)

15- In those days saw I in Judah some treading wine presses on the sabbath, and bringing in sheaves, and lading asses; as also wine, grapes, and figs, and all manner of burdens, which they brought into Jerusalem on the sabbath day: and I testified against them in the day wherein they sold victuals. 16- There dwelt men of Tyre also therein, which brought fish, and all manner of ware, and sold on the sabbath unto the children of Judah, and in Jerusalem. 17- Then I contended with the nobles of Judah, and said unto them, What evil thing is this that ye do, and profane the sabbath day? 18- Did not your fathers thus, and did not our God bring all this evil upon us, and upon this city? yet ye bring more wrath upon Israel by profaning the sabbath. 19- And it came to pass, that when the gates of Jerusalem began to be dark before the sabbath, I commanded that the gates should be shut, and charged that they should not be opened till after the sabbath: and some of my servants set I at the gates, that there should no burden be brought in on the sabbath day. 20- So the merchants and sellers of all kind of ware lodged without Jerusalem once or twice. 21- Then I testified against them, and said unto them, Why lodge ye about the wall? if ye do so again, I will lay hands on you. From that time forth came they no more on the sabbath. 22- And I commanded the Levites that they should cleanse themselves, and that they should come and keep the gates, to sanctify the sabbath day. Remember me, O my God, concerning this also, and spare me according to the greatness of thy mercy.

entries.section: (3) The portions of the priests and Levites

paragraphs.text: Nehemiah also noticed, as he went about in Jerusalem, that some of the Jews were treading grapes in the wine presses to press them, and this was on the Sabbath day, on which it is forbidden to do any material work, so that the Jews might devote themselves to the worship of God.

He also saw in the fields the farmers gathering the sheaves of their harvest and binding them, and the porters loading the donkeys with burdens to carry from place to place, and all these works were forbidden on the Sabbath day (Ex 34:21; Deut 5:14; Jer 17:21). The Jews do not work, and likewise they let their animals rest on the Sabbath day.

He also found on the Sabbath day Jews coming from the various lands to Jerusalem with wares of wine, grapes and figs to sell on that day, and of course trade was forbidden on the Sabbath day. Here appears the exactness of Nehemiah, who went about himself to care for his people and correct their errors, especially after he found the deviation of the priests under Eliashib and the slackness of the rulers. So he relied on himself in examining everything, until matters were put right, and after this each one would do his own work.

He declares clearly that he testified against them, that is, he made known to them their sin in breaking the Sabbath. He did not punish them, but taught them the Law and called them to follow it. In this he had no personal anger against them, but firmness in carrying out the commandment of God, which is the fourth of the Ten Commandments, which requires keeping the Sabbath (Ex 20:8).

entries.section: (3) The portions of the priests and Levites

paragraphs.text: Tyre was a coastal city on the Mediterranean Sea, and was the most famous city in the world in trade. Near it lay Sidon, famous for fishing, and they used to bring this fish to sell in Jerusalem. Because of the considerable distance between Tyre and Jerusalem, they most likely salted the fish so that it could endure the journey. These Tyrians had temporary dwellings in Jerusalem, but their permanent places of residence were in Tyre.

Because the Jews broke the Sabbath and sold and bought on it, this encouraged the Tyrians, that is, the Gentiles, to come to sell this fish and all their wares in Jerusalem and the surrounding cities.

entries.section: (3) The portions of the priests and Levites

paragraphs.text: Nehemiah stood as an adversary to the elders and leaders of the people, and rebuked them for breaking the fourth commandment of God, which is the sanctification of the Sabbath day for His worship; in this they profane the Sabbath day and anger God. Nehemiah here is a type of Christ the Judge, who will call all to account for their sins; for the sin of the leaders was not only that they sold and bought on the Sabbath, but that they allowed the people to do so, and so they made them stumble by this negligence. Their conduct may have led to negligence about the Sabbath by doing works other than trade.

entries.section: (3) The portions of the priests and Levites

paragraphs.text: Nehemiah added, and reminded the leaders that negligence in breaking the Sabbath and the other commandments of God is what brought the Babylonian captivity upon Jerusalem and Judea, after the kingdom of Israel had been taken captive. Because the people in ancient times neglected the rest of the seventh year and sowed the land against the commandment of God, the land enjoyed her sabbaths, that is, the land rested from cultivation for seventy years, the period of the Babylonian captivity, in place of the Jews' neglect of the commandment of the seventh year for 490 years (2 Chr 36:21). And Nehemiah said to the leaders before the people that by this they were increasing the wrath of God against His city Jerusalem. So the leaders and all the people wept because of their breaking of the Sabbath, and became ready to carry out the commandment.

entries.section: (3) The portions of the priests and Levites

paragraphs.text: Nehemiah took definite decisions concerning the keeping of the Sabbath, which were:
1- He testified, with his assistants, against the merchants who sold and bought on the Sabbath day (v. 15).
2- He rebuked the leaders, who represent all the people, for their breaking of the Sabbath day, and so exposing themselves to the divine wrath (vv. 17, 18).

3- At the end of Friday, when darkness covered the gates of Jerusalem, announcing the beginning of the night of the Sabbath, Nehemiah commanded that the gates be shut and not be opened until the whole Sabbath day had ended.
Then Nehemiah appointed some of his assistants as watchers over all the gates of Jerusalem, to make sure that the commandment to keep the Sabbath was carried out.

entries.section: (3) The portions of the priests and Levites

paragraphs.text: Although Nehemiah's orders were definite and strong, the merchants thought that it was merely a temporary severity on his part, which he would forget and be distracted from in time. So they came with their wares on the next Sabbath, but the gates of Jerusalem remained shut and no one entered. When this was repeated on the following Sabbath and Nehemiah learned of it, he testified against them concerning this sin, which was their intention to break the Sabbath.

Nehemiah was not content with this, but threatened them that if they came on the next Sabbath with wares and lodged outside the city at the gates, he would seize them and throw them into prison for attempting to break the Sabbath. Here we find Nehemiah's firmness in carrying out the commandment and his watching of the gates to prevent the breaking of the Sabbath, and even his threatening those who tried to break the commandment, so that he was able to end this evil within two weeks.
Be strict against sin and stop its sources, while examining yourself every day and committing yourself to the sacrament of confession, and you will be able to be rid of it by the power of God.

entries.section: (3) The portions of the priests and Levites

paragraphs.text: To keep the gates of Jerusalem shut continually on the Sabbath, Nehemiah appointed officials from the Levites over every gate, to guarantee that the commandment was carried out, and by this the people kept the Sabbath and devoted themselves in it to the worship of God.

Holding fast to this commandment continued from the days of Nehemiah, that is, in the fifth century before the birth of Christ, until the days of Christ, to the point that the scribes and Pharisees held literally to keeping the Sabbath with all exactness, so that they resisted Christ when they thought He had broken the Sabbath, although He did not break it in any material matters, but did good on the Sabbath, which is the healing of the sick.

Nehemiah ends his work in keeping the Sabbath with a prayer in which he asks God to bless him and have mercy on him and bless his holding fast to the commandment. This confirms that Nehemiah is a man of prayer and humble, who asks the compassion and mercies of God. He does not boast of doing good, but feels that he is a sinner in need of God's mercy.

Nehemiah asked the Levites to purify themselves, that is, to wash and wash their clothes and keep away from any uncleanness, before their guarding of the gates of Jerusalem, considering this guarding a holy work because it is the carrying out of the fourth commandment. So he made them feel the importance of guarding the gates, especially since he was about to return to the king after a while, and so would have placed this guard in faithful hands, namely the Levites, that they might keep the commandment out of their love for God.
(4) Separation from foreign marriages (vv. 23-31)
23- In those days also saw I Jews that had married wives of Ashdod, of Ammon, and of Moab:

24- And their children spake half in the speech of Ashdod, and could not speak in the Jews' language, but according to the language of each people. 25- And I contended with them, and cursed them, and smote certain of them, and plucked off their hair, and made them swear by God, saying, Ye shall not give your daughters unto their sons, nor take their daughters unto your sons, or for yourselves.

26- Did not Solomon king of Israel sin by these things? yet among many nations was there no king like him, who was beloved of his God, and God made him king over all Israel: nevertheless even him did outlandish women cause to sin. 27- Shall we then hearken unto you to do all this great evil, to transgress against our God in marrying strange wives? 28- And one of the sons of Joiada, the son of Eliashib the high priest, was son in law to Sanballat the Horonite: therefore I chased him from me.

29- Remember them, O my God, because they have defiled the priesthood, and the covenant of the priesthood, and of the Levites. 30- Thus cleansed I them from all strangers, and appointed the wards of the priests and the Levites, every one in his business; 31- And for the wood offering, at times appointed, and for the firstfruits. Remember me, O my God, for good.

entries.section: (3) The portions of the priests and Levites

paragraphs.text: In negligence the people of God disobeyed their Law and married idolatrous women from the lands surrounding them. One was Ashdod, which is one of the five great cities of the Philistines, lying on the Mediterranean Sea, that is, west of the dwelling of the people of God and beside it, adjoining it. They also married from Moab and the children of Ammon, two peoples who dwell east of the land of the Jews and adjoining it.

These marriages led to the begetting of children who could not speak well the language of the people of God, which is the Hebrew language, which they had kept throughout the period of the captivity. The language of Ashdod is close in pronunciation to Hebrew but differs from it, and Nehemiah was greatly distressed when he noticed this strange speech spread among the people of God.

It is noted that Ezra, some years earlier, had played a great part in keeping away from the foreign wives (Ezra 9, 10), but they were negligent and went back to these marriages. So the importance of Nehemiah's following up the carrying out of the Law appeared, in this matter in particular, which sadly leads to the worship of idols, since the people worship the idolatrous gods in honor of their wives.

entries.section: (3) The portions of the priests and Levites

paragraphs.text: Nehemiah saw the people's absorption in marrying idolatrous women and their attachment to them to the point that separation was difficult, so he carried out the Law as it is (Deut 7:3) and did these things with them in order to separate them from the foreign women:
1- He contended with them, that is, he stood as an adversary to them, declaring the Law of God which condemns them.
2- He cursed them, that is, he declared to them the divine curses which they deserved for breaking the Law.
3- He smote them as the Law prescribed (Deut 25:2, 3), and of course this smiting was done through his assistants.
4- He plucked off their hair, and this was not only discipline but contempt for them, because the hair of the beard represents the awe and respect due to elders.

5- He made them swear, that is, he made them take an oath to separate from marriage with the foreign women, and not to marry any foreign women afterward, or allow their children to enter these sinful marriages.

And this making them swear is what the Law prescribed (Deut 7:3). By this he placed these men who had transgressed the Law face to face with God, so that they would afterward fear breaking the Law, and if they broke it they would deserve punishment.

entries.section: (3) The portions of the priests and Levites

paragraphs.text: Nehemiah showed the people the seriousness of marriage with foreign women: not only that it is against the Law of God (v. 25), but he also gave a practical example of the hideousness of this sin, which is what happened with King Solomon, who was beloved of God, but this sin brought the wrath of God upon him. Adversaries to him appeared in his kingdom who rebelled against him, although he was king over all Israel, and the kingdom was divided after him, because he pleased his idolatrous wives and made images of strange gods in Jerusalem, which greatly provoked God. Thus he lost his greatness in wisdom and wealth because of his attachment to idolatrous women. Therefore every person is exposed to ruin if he is attached to idolatry, because he is no better than Solomon, who was very wise.

entries.section: (3) The portions of the priests and Levites

paragraphs.text: Because of all that preceded concerning the seriousness of the sin of attachment to idolaters, Nehemiah declared that he would not keep silent about this existing evil, that is, the strange marriages that were before him at that time. Nehemiah had persuaded the people of the decision he would take, which was separation from the idolatrous women, before he took the decision. Thus Nehemiah's ability in managing the affairs of the kingdom appears, even in the hardest matters, which were the existing marriages that had produced forbidden children, because he persuaded the people that it was a great treachery against God.

entries.section: (3) The portions of the priests and Levites

paragraphs.text: Nehemiah's courage appeared when he found one of the grandsons of the high priest Eliashib married to an idolatrous woman, the daughter of Sanballat the Horonite, who had resisted Nehemiah in the building of the wall. He rebuked him and asked him to separate from his wife and return to God, but he refused, so Nehemiah was compelled to drive him out of the priesthood and from membership in the people of God. Sanballat received him with welcome, as Josephus the historian mentions, and built him a temple in which to serve idolatrous gods on Mount Gerizim, and the name of this priest was Manasseh. Perhaps this mountain is what is meant in the words of the Samaritan woman with Christ (Jn 4:20).

entries.section: (3) The portions of the priests and Levites

paragraphs.text: Nehemiah was in great anger because of the defilement of this place, and perhaps there were with him other priests and Levites who had also entered idolatrous marriages. It was expected of the priests and Levites that they would be an example to the people in holding fast to the Law. Therefore Nehemiah asked God to remember them, to warn them to repent of their evil and separate from marriages with idolatrous women, or to allow them afflictions, perhaps so that they might feel the hideousness of their sins and repent. It also means Nehemiah's appeal to the justice of God, who punishes those who persist in breaking His Law.

entries.section: (3) The portions of the priests and Levites

paragraphs.text: Nehemiah purified the whole people from every strange marriage by separating from these wives and keeping away from them, and whoever persisted in his attachment to his wife he drove out and set apart from the people of God. After the driving out of those who persisted in evil, the service was not shaken, for Nehemiah redistributed the priests and Levites to their various services to fill the place of those who persisted in the idolatrous marriage and kept away from the service. So he organized the service of guarding, the offering of wood and the collecting of the firstfruits, each offering at its time, and likewise all the works of service inside the Temple.

In the end Nehemiah, the man of prayer, lifts up his heart to God, seeking from Him blessing and good, for he does all this for Him alone and asks nothing for himself, because his good comes to him from God.

Beware of being attached to any person who draws you away from God, whatever the motives, for the salvation of your soul is more important than anything in the world. And if you have become attached, ask the help of God, that you may courageously be rid of what hinders your spiritual growth.
A summary of the most important personalities in the life of Nehemiah
1- Nehemiah is a Hebrew word meaning “Yahweh has shown compassion.”
2- He was born in the captivity, and God gave him a high position with King Artaxerxes, namely the king's cupbearer.
3- He loved God, and his position in the Persian state did not distract him from his worship of God, his prayers and his fasts.

4- His heart was attached to the holy city Jerusalem and the house of the Lord that is in it, so he inquired of his brethren the Jews who had visited Jerusalem about its news, and when he learned that its walls were broken down and its gates burned, he was deeply moved, wept and prayed much to God.

5- Nehemiah the son of Hachaliah was not a priest like Ezra, or a prophet like Haggai, or of the royal seed like Zerubbabel; he was an ordinary Jewish person who obtained a great position in the state, but his heart was attached to God and he felt his responsibility toward the holy city Jerusalem.

6- He was distinguished by courage, for he did not hide his sorrow when he stood to perform his office before the king, although this exposed him to great danger; but because he prayed, God gave him favor in the eyes of the king, who asked him the reason for his sorrow, and when he learned it he sympathized with him and heard his requests and fulfilled them all for him, for the care of Jerusalem (ch. 1).

7- He led the third company returning from the captivity to Jerusalem, and that was in the year 445 BC, thirteen years after the return of Ezra. Its number was small and the exact number is not mentioned, and he had with him a permit from the king to obtain timber for the gates of Jerusalem from the king's forests (ch. 2:8).

8- He inspected the wall of Jerusalem as soon as he arrived, organized the work of building the wall among the clans of the Jews, and encouraged the people with great zeal, so that he was able to build the wall in 52 days (ch. 6:15), and he dedicated the wall in a great celebration (ch. 12).

9- He faced violent resistance from the enemies of the Jews who dwelt around him, but he was strong and continued the work with courage, and God revealed their tricks to him, so they did not hinder him from completing the wall (ch. 3, 4, 6).

10- He remained governor over Jerusalem and Judea for twelve years, after which he returned to Shushan, the palace, the capital of the Persian state, and then returned a second time to complete his rule and his care for his people (ch. 5:14).

11- He relied on prayer together with work in building the wall and preparing for war by bearing arms to defend Jerusalem before the enemies; that is, prayer was joined with striving and work (ch. 3, 4, 6), and he offered a fervent prayer for himself and his people (ch. 9).
12- He took care to solve the internal problems of the people, that is, sympathy for the poor and for those enslaved by their fellow Jews (ch. 5:1-6).

13- He was distinguished by giving and generosity and by not exploiting the poor people to take from them the money assigned to the governor; rather he spent from the funds of his position in the Persian state, and made tables for those gathered with him in the governor's palace (ch. 5:14-19).
14- After the building of the wall Nehemiah took care to organize the guarding of the city of Jerusalem (ch. 7).
15- He took care to establish the genealogies of those returning from the captivity and to repopulate the city of Jerusalem with inhabitants from the returnees (ch. 7).

16- Nehemiah was a wise manager, as appeared in his talk with the king, for he presented his requests in a definite form; and when he reached Jerusalem he inspected the wall, made a plan for the building, organized the building companies and the places of repair, followed the work himself, and faced the resistance of the enemies with divine wisdom, so that he was not hindered from his work.

17- He took care of the spiritual life of his people, and Ezra the priest shared this with him, so he read to them the book of the Law and organized the celebration of the Feast of Tabernacles (ch. 8).

18- After his return from Shushan (the capital of the Persian state) to Jerusalem, Nehemiah took care of the internal reforms: he took care of collecting the tithes and establishing the Levites in their service, purified the Temple of the vessels and belongings of Tobiah the Ammonite, the enemy of the people of God, sanctified the Sabbath day and prevented trade in it (ch. 13).

19- He was firm with those who had married idolatrous women, so he rebuked them and punished them, because they had returned to this sin after Ezra had warned them more than thirteen years earlier (ch. 13).
20- He was a contemporary of the prophet Malachi, the last of the prophets of the Old Testament, who prophesied around the year 433 BC.

21- Nehemiah remained governor of Jerusalem for twelve years, during which he built the wall and carried out his spiritual reforms, then returned to Shushan, the palace, for a short time, and came back to Jerusalem to correct the spiritual errors into which they had fallen in the period of his absence, and remained governor over Jerusalem, caring for it civilly and spiritually. Types of Christ and the Church. Nehemiah is a type of Christ
1- Building:
Nehemiah took care to build the wall of Jerusalem and its broken-down gates (ch. 6:15), and Christ rebuilt our nature by His redemption and made us living stones in His Church.
2- Asceticism:

Nehemiah was distinguished by contentment, so he gave up what was collected from the people for the governor and spent from his own funds for the needy (ch. 5:14, 16), and Christ was born in a manger and lived poor and took care to feed the crowds by blessing the two fish and the five loaves and the seven loaves and the few small fish.
3- Prayer:
It is mentioned of Nehemiah in his book that he prayed ten times, and Christ would withdraw and spend the whole night in prayer.
4- Order:
Nehemiah divided the Jews into groups in the building of the wall (ch. 3), and Christ made the crowds sit down by fifties and by hundreds when He fed them with the fish and the bread.
5- Firmness:

Nehemiah threw Tobiah's belongings outside the Temple, shut the gates of Jerusalem on the Sabbath, threatened the merchants who lodged outside the city on the Sabbath, and drove the priests who had made strange marriages away from service in the Temple (ch. 13), and Christ drove the sellers out of the Temple and pronounced the woes upon the scribes and Pharisees.
6- Self-giving:
Nehemiah gave up his position in the king's palace and went to labor in Jerusalem to build the wall. And Christ left His heavenly glory, became incarnate and redeemed us on the Cross.
7- Weeping over Jerusalem:
Nehemiah mourned when he heard of the broken-down walls of Jerusalem and the burned gates (ch. 1), and Christ wept over Jerusalem, which was spiritually broken down because it refused repentance.
8- Resisting Satan:

Nehemiah endured the resistance of the wicked until he completed the building of the wall (ch. 3-6), and Christ endured the temptation on the mountain and all the resistance of the scribes, the Pharisees and the priests.
